description: Snowflake's structured-nullability DDL rule, one measured CREATE per cell: a NOT NULL field inside a structured type is legal only when everything enclosing it is itself non-nullable (per LEVEL - nested objects need every level NOT NULL, the path prefixing the upper-cased column and keeping field names verbatim), and never inside an ARRAY (.element path) or MAP (.value path) whatever the column's own nullability; structured types without NOT NULL fields are untouched. Converted 1:1 from expressions/StructuredNullabilityDdlTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE nn_flat (nn OBJECT(x VARCHAR NOT NULL))

error.messageContains: DDL operation failed because it would result in a non-nullable structured type field 'NN.x' contained within a nullable object

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE nn_ok (nn OBJECT(x VARCHAR NOT NULL) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE nn_nested (o OBJECT(inner OBJECT(x INT NOT NULL)) NOT NULL)

error.messageContains: non-nullable structured type field 'O.inner.x' contained within a nullable object

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE nn_nested_ok (o OBJECT(inner OBJECT(x INT NOT NULL) NOT NULL) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE nn_arr (na ARRAY(OBJECT(x INT NOT NULL)))

error.messageContains: non-nullable structured type field 'NA.element.x' contained within an array or map

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE nn_arr2 (na ARRAY(OBJECT(x INT NOT NULL)) NOT NULL)

error.messageContains: non-nullable structured type field 'NA.element.x' contained within an array or map

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE nn_arr3 (o OBJECT(a ARRAY(OBJECT(x INT NOT NULL))) NOT NULL)

error.messageContains: non-nullable structured type field 'O.a.element.x' contained within an array or map

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE nn_map (mm MAP(VARCHAR, OBJECT(x INT NOT NULL)))

error.messageContains: non-nullable structured type field 'MM.value.x' contained within an array or map

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE nn_map2 (mm MAP(VARCHAR, OBJECT(x INT NOT NULL)) NOT NULL)

error.messageContains: non-nullable structured type field 'MM.value.x' contained within an array or map

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE nn_plain (o OBJECT(x INT, y VARCHAR), na ARRAY(OBJECT(x INT)), mm MAP(VARCHAR, ARRAY(INT)))
